responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the AArch64 architecture, covering machine-specific compilation from target option parsing through RTL generation, scheduling, hardening, and final assembly conventions. Its core files (`aarch64.cc`/`.h`, `aarch64.md`, `aarch64.opt`, and shared prototypes/defs) define AArch64 ISA and ABI rules, register and addressing behavior, instruction patterns, machine modes, constraints, atomics, costing, and target hooks; large builtin families implement the user-visible ACLE and target intrinsic interfaces for scalar AArch64 features, AdvSIMD/NEON, SVE, SVE2, SME, and NEON-SVE bridging, together with the installed `arm_*` headers and C/D front-end glue. The module also contains AArch64-specific RTL passes and hardening support such as BTI insertion, speculation tracking, CC fusion, early register allocation, FMA steering, and load/store-pair or Falkor tuning passes; per-core scheduler and tuning models for many CPUs; driver-side native CPU detection and architecture/extension tables; and OS/ABI subtarget headers for ELF, COFF/Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, NetBSD, GNU/Hurd, RTEMS, VxWorks, and bi-ABI variants. Overall, this directory is the complete AArch64 code-generation and target-integration subsystem that distinguishes AArch64 behavior from generic GCC middle-end logic and from other target backends.
